# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Suspicious Child Process of a WinRM Session Host** · `T1021.006_wsmprovhost_suspicious_child` · [T1021.006](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/006/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1021.006_wsmprovhost_suspicious_child for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     ParentImage=<value>  Image=<value>  OriginalFileName=<value>  CommandLine=<value>
Checked:      1. Identify the source host and account of the WinRM session (Security 4624 type 3 on the target just before) -> <result>
              2. Read the full command line of the child and its own children -> <result>
              3. Check whether this account normally administers this host over WinRM -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | management_script_share (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Administrators running cmd.exe commands or batch files over PowerShell remoting or winrs
- Configuration management that launches cmd.exe through WinRM
- Ansible's WinRM connection, which starts cmd /C PowerShell ... -EncodedCommand under winrshost.exe on every managed host (public data: the labs' provisioning)

Never tune:
- Never filter encoded PowerShell or the proxy binaries (rundll32, regsvr32, mshta, certutil, bitsadmin) under a WinRM host in general. The one exception is a reviewed automation bootstrap (for example Ansible's), excepted in the SIEM by its source host together with its exact command line.
- Never filter by account alone - a stolen administrator account is exactly what this rule must catch.


Escalate when any of these holds:
1. Encoded PowerShell or a proxy binary under wsmprovhost.exe or winrshost.exe, other than a documented automation bootstrap from its known host
2. The source host or account has never used WinRM against this target
3. The session ran discovery or credential commands (whoami /all, net group, nltest)

Risk conditions: user is privileged +15 · host is critical +15 · payload in user writable path +10 · outside business hours +10 · approved admin activity -25 · approved change window -20.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Disable or reset the account used for the session
2. Isolate the source host if it is not an administration host
3. Block WinRM (TCP 5985/5986) from that source until reviewed
